contract:
FOLD THIS SIGNAL (plain text, no em-dashes, under 150 words): the row below is a signal an estate captured. Answer three things only: (1) TRUE-TODAY: is this signal still true given everything else you know in the row's context - yes/no/unknown with one line of why; (2) THE ORGAN: which kind of organ should own this signal (a law, a clock, a gate, a memory row, or compost); (3) THE FALSIFIER: the observation that would prove the signal wrong. Mark unknowns UNKNOWN; do not pad.

SIGNAL: A “deniable‑yet‑verifiable” channel is required for the Frontier‑Scout “Burn” pipeline. Authenticated messages must be verifiable by the intended peer but must leave no transferable proof of authorship to any third party. Public‑key signatures are disallowed because they are inherently transferable. The design must rely on a symmetric MAC that both endpoints can compute, satisfying the deniability axiom (any valid (message, tag) pair can be simulated by either side). Security‑protocol designer tasked with specifying a concrete, buildable deniable authentication mechanism. Provide **THE MECHANI
